title: The things that keep going while you do something else
target: How vending machines and the back-room racks are tracked in Supermarket Simulator, so the parts of the shop that run on their own can be checked from wherever you are.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: At least one vending machine placed
The computer or tablet to check from

steps.do: Know that a machine can be watched from elsewhere.
steps.because: there is a tracker and a tracker object for vending machines (VendingMachineTracker, VendingMachineTrackerObject)

steps.do: Look for the machine on the map rather than walking to it.
steps.because: each machine has an object of its own for the mini-map (VendingMachineMiniMapObject)

steps.do: Read what a machine holds from its container rather than from the machine.
steps.because: what a machine holds is kept in a container and the tracker's data has a list of its own (VendingContainer, VendingDataListWrapper)

steps.do: On a controller, use the tracker panel's own handlers.
steps.because: the tracker panel is built for a controller, with handlers for the panel and for what it shows (VendingTrackerPanelGamepadHandler, VendingTrackerProductGamepadHandler)

steps.do: Treat a back-room rack as a recorded thing rather than as furniture.
steps.because: a rack has data of its own and is also defined by a definition object (RackData, RackSO)

steps.do: Know that a box on a rack and a box on a stand are kept apart.
steps.because: a box on a rack is recorded on its own and a box on a stand is recorded separately (RackedBoxData, StandBoxData)

steps.do: Expect being racked to be a state.
steps.because: a box on a rack is an object of its own and being racked is a state (RackBox, RackingState)

steps.do: Remember the back room as a whole has its own record.
steps.because: storage has data of its own (StorageData)

commonMistakes: Walking to a vending machine to check it when the tracker exists.
Assuming a box is recorded the same way whether it is on a rack or on a stand.
Treating the back room as one pile rather than as recorded racks and boxes.
Looking for a machine's contents on the machine instead of in its container.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
